newsitem.title: UK: Euro products outlook - Transatlantic trade key.
newsitem.headline: Euro products outlook - Transatlantic trade key.

text.p: Transatlantic trade will be a major factor in European oil product markets this week as the U.S. draws gasoline stocks out of the region and gas oil faces the uphill task of absorbing U.S. barrels heading into Europe.
Portuguese and Tunisian purchase tenders will underpin fuel oil, traders said, while good petrochemical demand will support naphtha given the high prices for alternative feedstock LPG.
Reduced European refinery maintenance, expected to run at just half of 1995 levels between September and November, should ensure current product tightness is not exacerbated.
Around 350,000 bpd of capacity is set to shut in October and in November following a 600,000 barrels per day shortfall in September, the International Energy Agency recently estimated.
Light oil products remain well supported because of an attractive arbitrage to the U.S. which has absorbed around half a million tonnes of September-loading gasoline and a few cargoes of naphtha.
Europe's gasoline barge market, however, is well supplied, with inventory levels up on week-ago and year-ago levels.
This will continue to weigh on local prices, currently at $200 a tonne fob ARA.
The unusually wide spread between Eurograde and regular gasoline should remain in place, with good demand for higher octane barrels in Lavera and Poland.

Trader buying has levered naphtha well above gasoline numbers, dampening refiner demand. But soaring LPG prices, largely as a result of low U.S. stocks, mean petrochemical demand for naphtha will remain strong.

Strong gas oil may by the end start to feel the impact of the first of about ten north American gas oil cargoes, amounting to roughly 400,000 tonnes, heading to hit Europe. The influx might temporarily cut physical gas oil premiums $1-$2.
"The U.S. material could push down premiums but there's still a lot of restocking to be done in Europe and once the cold begins to bite demand can only grow," another trader said.

High sulphur cracked fuel oil is likely to remain tight in both NWE and the Med with prices steady or a touch firmer. The latest Portuguese high sulphur fuel oil tender for up to 150,000 tonnes will probably be sourced from both regions. Tunisia is looking for two cargoes in October in addition to the 200,000 tonnes it tendered for from now until January.
Traders thought high sulphur cargoes might rise $1-$2 over Friday's range of $109-110 fob NWE.
The high to low sulphur spread could narrow this week as high sulphur rises to meet steady low sulphur levels.

"I see low sulphur staying steady with the spread narrowing as high sulphur rises," said a broker. An increase in low sulphur demand from the main Med buyer ENEL could be countered by Caribbean supplies. Both high and low sulphur should be able to resist softer crude unless the drop is dramatic.
"Fuel does have room to move down," said one trader.
